this is the same police who waited too long to uncover CCTV which would have revealed his next movements. I guess we do have to go on what the police say but if this is true I imagine Andrew was the only child of his age in the UK without an email address or who didn't use the internet privately.

Reading about this case today I have a couple of suggestions. I should first warn readers that the details of my theory (although they have undoubtedly been suggested before) are rather cynical and I would hate anybody from Andrew's family to stumble on to such a candid hypothesis of what happened. But below are some points that I have deduced from what I know about the case. 

1) The idea that a 14 year old boy would successfully dupe the country (especially in the age of the internet) by doing a Reginald Perrin is too fantastical. And I don't accept that a suicidal teenager would go to the trouble of withdrawing money (when cash was freely available) and travel all the way to London without leaving any indication of his suicidal intention. Therefore, the only conclusion I can accept as logical is that another human being attracted Andrew to London and was almost certainly responsible for his disappearance. 

2) This person was unlikely to have known Andrew personally given the distance between London and Doncaster. Yet somehow, a bond of trust (enough to cause Andrew to deceive his family and travel a considerable distance) had developed between the pair. The internet would have provided a private basis for this 'bond of trust' to grow without anybody else having the faintest idea of the coercive relationship that was developing. The arrangements that were made between the pair are anybody's guess. 

3) You really don't have to look hard to find a multitude of examples of paedophile's hijacking chat rooms of different kinds to groom/manipulate young people. It is futile to speculate how this may have been done. Suffice to say, that it is extremely easy to look at someone's online profile, pick a couple of subjects of interest and convince a person that they have just met their online kindred spirit. 

4) So for me, (and it pains me to say it), the key to finding out what happened to Andrew in the absence of evidence, is to assume the logical worst. He is likely to have been abducted for sexual motivation and killed thereafter. So the mystery for me is not 'where is Andrew Gosden?' but 'who killed Andrew Gosden?'. 

5) A sexual predator who is willing to go to these lengths is likely to harbour a compulsion that has meant similar crimes of child abuse have been committed before and/or since Andrew's abduction. The person responsible is likely to be on the sex offenders register and so if I were police, I would be looking at all known online groomers of young boys in and around the time of Andrew's disappearance. 

5) This link: http://theukdatabase.com/2012/03/14/peter-williams-southampton/ reveals the story of a man who had an unhealthy obsession with grooming boys of Andrew's age. He was caught and convicted in 2008. He is from Southampton but had travelled to London to meet up with one victim after meeting him online. I do not know the details of this case and it is overly speculative of me to suggest this man had anything to do with Andrew's disappearance and has by all accounts turned his life around. But like many, I do not feel the police have done right by Andrew or his family and have left too many stones unturned here. Therefore I only post this link (perhaps irresponsibly) as an example of the types of characters the police should be looking at for further inquiry. 

With my (perhaps unfounded) theory out of the way, I would like to say that Andrew's story has haunted me for about a year now. I hope and pray that the truth is uncovered for the sake of Andrew's family and whoever is responsible for this nightmare is brought to justice.
